proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a deterministic binary schedule \(Y\).  For a cluster \(c\) of response type \(t_c^\star=t\) and a policy \(r\), exact second-stage randomization gives
\[
 \Pr(Z_{ci}=1\mid R_c=r)=\frac{k_r}{n}
 \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
\]
because each of the \(\binom n{k_r}\) subsets is equally likely and \(\binom{n-1}{k_r-1}/\binom n{k_r}=k_r/n\).  Fixed potential outcomes and stratified interference therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 W_{cr}
 &:=\mathbb E_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left[
      \frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}Y_{ci}(Z_{ci},r)
      \;\middle|\;R_c=r\right]\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
   \left\{\left(1-\frac{k_r}{n}\right)Y_{ci}(0,r)
          +\frac{k_r}{n}Y_{ci}(1,r)\right\}\\
 &=\frac{(n-k_r)(N_{c,r}^{10}+N_{c,r}^{11})
          +k_r(N_{c,r}^{01}+N_{c,r}^{11})}{n^2}
 =u_{t_c^\star r}=u_{tr}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The conditioning event has positive probability because \(m_r\ge1\) and the uniform exact first stage gives \(\Pr(R_c=r)=m_r/C>0\).  The displayed expression is the design-average outcome under the intervention that assigns quota policy \(r\) to cluster \(c\), and the interior-quota condition ensures every unit has both own-treatment states in the second-stage support.  Averaging over the fixed clusters and grouping equal response types yields
\[
 \frac1C\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}W_{cr}
 =\frac1C\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}N_t^\star u_{tr}
 =U_r(N^\star).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal O(N^\star)\) is the complete weak order of fixed finite-population causal policy welfares.  The empirical vector \(\widehat U(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is only a randomization statistic and is not being identified with that causal vector.

By \(\texttt{lem:true-counts-compatible}\),
\(N^\star\in\mathcal N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) for every realization.  Hence the definition of the confidence set gives
\[
 \{p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\}
 \subseteq
 \{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\]
Taking complements and applying \(\texttt{lem:schedule-pvalue-valid}\) with \(N=N^\star\) and \(q=\alpha\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
   \mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
   \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})
 \right\}
 &\le
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\!\left\{
   p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\le\alpha
 \right\}\\
 &\le\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This argument is pointwise in \(Y\), so the lower coverage bound is uniform over all schedules satisfying the four stated assumptions.  The cited super-uniformity result already permits discrete and degenerate randomization distributions; consequently no continuity, positive-variance, rank, or limiting condition is used.

For the reporting corollary, represent a retained weak order as descending tied blocks \((B_1,\ldots,B_J)\).  If \(r\in B_j\), define its occupied-position interval by
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r)
 =\left\{1+\sum_{\ell<j}|B_\ell|,\ldots,
              \sum_{\ell\le j}|B_\ell|\right\}.
\]
On the coverage event the true weak order is retained, and therefore, simultaneously for every \(r\in\mathcal R\),
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O(N^\star)}(r)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{\mathcal O\in
   \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})}
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r).
\]
This is precisely simultaneous containment of all true tied-rank intervals.

theorem.statement:
Use \(L_N(H)\) and \(\delta_\star\) from \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\).  Fix \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\).  Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) be any deterministic map from arm-outcome tables to sets of complete weak orders such that, for every fixed binary schedule satisfying the design and stratified-interference assumptions,
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
If \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) for every compatible \(H\), then in fact
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 \qquad\text{for every compatible }H.
\]
More sharply, if \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\), there is a deterministic schedule realizing \(N\) for which the noncoverage probability is at least
\[
 L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\]
Thus no family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) can both preserve uniform coverage at every level and be a strict contained refinement at some compatible table at every level.  This obstruction does not assert impossibility of a consonant strict refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\).  Every abstract response type is realized by a deterministic binary cluster schedule: for each \(t\in\mathcal T\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\), partition the labeled unit set \(\mathcal I\) into four sets \(I_{t,r}^{ab}\) of respective cardinalities \(N_r^{ab}\), and set
\[
 (Y_i(0,r),Y_i(1,r))=(a,b)
 \qquad\text{for }i\in I_{t,r}^{ab}.
\]
The partitions may be chosen separately across \(r\), because stratified interference imposes no cross-policy restriction on these fixed potential outcomes.  Put copies of this schedule on exactly \(N_t\) labeled clusters.  The resulting schedule is binary, satisfies the stated interference condition, and has true response-count vector \(N^\star=N\).  Under the exact two-stage design, \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) gives
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}=L_N(H).
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\).  On the event \(H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\), the realized schedule has true order \(\mathcal O(N^\star)=\mathcal O(N)\), so that event is contained in the noncoverage event.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)
        \notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}
 &\ge \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}\\
 &=L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This contradicts the assumed uniform coverage.  Therefore a uniformly valid \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) must contain \(\mathcal O(N)\) for every \(N\in\mathcal N(H)\) and every compatible \(H\).  The global-atom lemma gives
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}
\]
at the present \(\alpha\).  Combining the required inclusion \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) with the just-proved reverse inclusion gives equality at every compatible table.

The theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\) verifies that the baseline set itself attains the stated uniform coverage.  Since the preceding equality is forced for every \(\alpha\in(0,\delta_\star)\), a family required to be strictly smaller at some compatible table at every nominal level cannot exist.  No step treats \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), so no conclusion about that regime follows.
theorem.justification: The finite exact design has a positive global minimum observation-atom size, which forces any uniformly valid contained procedure to retain every compatible order at sufficiently small \(\alpha\).
theorem.gap: The requested strict consonant refinement cannot hold uniformly at every nominal level: strictness is impossible for \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\), while the existence question for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\) remains unresolved.
theorem.consumer: Exact-order software can compute \(\delta_\star\) and certify the levels at which the unrefined compatible-order report is forced by finite-sample coverage.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(h\in\mathcal H(N)\), define its coarsening by
\[
 \Gamma(h)=\left(\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}h_{trx}\right)_{r\in\mathcal R,\,x\in\mathcal X_n}.
\]
Let
\[
 \mathfrak J=\left\{(H,N):
 H\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal R\times\mathcal X_n},\ 
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X_n}H_{rx}=m_r\ \text{for every }r,\ 
 \mathcal N(H)\ne\varnothing,\ N\in\mathcal N(H)\right\},
\]
and, for \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\), set
\[
 L_N(H)=\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H(N)\\ \Gamma(h)=H}}\mathsf P_N(h),
 \qquad
 \delta_\star=\min_{(H,N)\in\mathfrak J}L_N(H).
\]
Then \(\mathfrak J\) is finite and nonempty, every \(L_N(H)\) is a strictly positive rational number equal to the design probability of observing \(H\) under a realizing population with count vector \(N\), and
\[
 0<\delta_\star\le1.
\]
Moreover, for every \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\),
\[
 p_N(H)\ge L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star.
\]
Consequently, for every \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\) and every compatible \(H\),
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H)
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}.
\]
The number \(\delta_\star\) is computable by finite exact-rational enumeration of the displayed joint set.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(t^0\in\mathcal T\) be the all-zero response type: for every \(r\), take \(N_r^{00}=n\) and \(N_r^{ab}=0\) for \((a,b)\ne(0,0)\).  The exact kernel formula gives \(Q_{t^0r}(0)=1\).  Define \(N^0_{t^0}=C\), with all other components zero, and define \(H^0_{r0}=m_r\), with all other cells zero.  The fine table having \(h^0_{t^0r0}=m_r\) and all other cells zero witnesses \(N^0\in\mathcal N(H^0)\).  Thus \(\mathfrak J\ne\varnothing\).  Both the arm-outcome table space and the count-vector space are finite because their entries are nonnegative integers with fixed total \(C\), so \(\mathfrak J\) is finite.

Fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\).  By compatibility there is a nonnegative integer array \(G\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_tG_{trx}=H_{rx},\qquad
 \sum_{r,x}G_{trx}=N_t,
 \qquad
 G_{trx}=0\ \text{if }Q_{tr}(x)=0.
\]
Because \(H\) has arm totals \(m_r\),
\[
 \sum_{t,x}G_{trx}=\sum_xH_{rx}=m_r,
\]
and hence \(G\in\mathcal H(N)\) and \(\Gamma(G)=H\).  Whenever \(G_{trx}>0\), compatibility gives \(Q_{tr}(x)>0\).  For cells with \(G_{trx}=0\), the factor \(Q_{tr}(x)^0\) is defined as one, including when \(Q_{tr}(x)=0\).  All factorials in the exact table mass are positive, so
\[
 \mathsf P_N(G)
 =\frac{\prod_tN_t!\prod_rm_r!}{C!\prod_{t,r,x}G_{trx}!}
   \prod_{t,r,x}Q_{tr}(x)^{G_{trx}}>0.
\]
Therefore \(L_N(H)\ge\mathsf P_N(G)>0\).

The count vector \(N\) is realized by an actual deterministic schedule.  Indeed, for each \(t\in\mathcal T\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\), partition \(\mathcal I\) into four sets of cardinalities \(N_r^{ab}\) and assign the pair \((Y_i(0,r),Y_i(1,r))=(a,b)\) on the corresponding set.  Such a partition exists because \(\sum_{a,b}N_r^{ab}=n\); it may be selected independently for different \(r\) because the stratified-interference schedule imposes no cross-policy equality.  Making exactly \(N_t\) clusters of each type \(t\) gives a binary fixed schedule with response-count vector \(N\).

By \(\texttt{lem:exact-table-law}\), the fine response-type/arm/outcome table has mass \(\mathsf P_N\) on \(\mathcal H(N)\).  The observed arm-outcome table is its coarsening \(\Gamma(h)\), so disjoint summation gives
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp},N}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}
 =\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H(N)\\\Gamma(h)=H}}
   \mathsf P_N(h)
 =L_N(H).
\]
The kernel probabilities are ratios of integers, so each mass and each finite sum is rational.  Since \(L_N(H)\) is also a probability, it lies in \((0,1]\).  A minimum over the nonempty finite set \(\mathfrak J\) is attained and remains strictly positive, proving \(0<\delta_\star\le1\).

Finally, if \(\Gamma(h)=H\), then the statistic in the right tail defining \(p_N(H)\) satisfies
\[
 S_N(\Gamma(h))=S_N(H).
\]
Every such fine table is therefore included in that weak right tail, whence
\[
 p_N(H)
 \ge\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H(N)\\\Gamma(h)=H}}
       \mathsf P_N(h)
 =L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star.
\]
If \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\), every \(N\in\mathcal N(H)\) passes the strict rule \(p_N(H)>\alpha\).  The reverse inclusion is built into the definition of \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha\), so
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H)
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}.
\]
All index sets and summands in the definition of \(\delta_\star\) are finite and rational, which also proves the asserted computability.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) satisfying the stated design and stratified-interference conditions,
\[
\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
The covered object is the complete weak order, so the assertion simultaneously covers all policy ranks, every partial tie pattern, and every zero-variance face. No pairwise allocation of \(\alpha\) and no cross-arm covariance estimator enters the construction. As an immediate reporting corollary, for each \(r\in\mathcal R\), take the union of the integer positions occupied by \(r\) over the retained weak orders, letting a tied block contribute every position that it spans. With the same probability, these rank sets simultaneously contain every policy's true tied-rank interval.
proposed.justification: This is the missing finite-sample simultaneous coverage theorem for exact-quota policy rankings.
proposed.gap: Mogstad et al. require a valid simultaneous difference region, Rigdon and Hudgens cover scalar effects, and Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong reserve finite-sample validity for stronger individual-level restrictions rather than the weak average welfare order.
proposed.consumer: RCT2 and the Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--Özler design calculator can report which complete and tied policy orderings remain compatible with the realized experiment at level \(1-\alpha\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof must cite the frozen response-type and welfare constructions that establish that the covered order is causal; this corrects dependency metadata without changing the claim.

prose_updates.tldr: The exact response-table inversion covers the complete finite-population causal welfare weak order with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over deterministic binary stratified-interference schedules, including ties and zero-variance faces. A new global atom calculation sets \(\delta_\star=\min_{(H,N)}L_N(H)>0\) over the finite joint set of compatible observations and response-count populations. For every \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\), any deterministic confidence set that is contained in the baseline set and retains uniform coverage must equal the baseline set at every compatible table. Thus strict refinement at every nominal level is impossible; consonant strict refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\) is not ruled out.

project_justification.fill: The core defines a max-discrepancy schedule-level randomization \(p\)-value, inverts it over compatible response counts, and retains precisely the weak orders not rejected. The exact factorial table law proves finite-sample simultaneous coverage, while the response-table quotient supplies a finite exact algorithm. The global compatible-atom bound additionally gives a computable threshold \(\delta_\star\): below it, every compatible order has too much probability mass to be omitted by any uniformly valid contained procedure.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite reference algorithm has the explicit response-table arithmetic bound \(O(K|\mathcal T|n^4+(d+K^2)B_NB_H)\), where \(d=K(n+1)|\mathcal T|\), \(B_N=\binom{C+|\mathcal T|-1}{|\mathcal T|-1}\), and \(B_H=\binom{C+d-1}{d-1}\); bit complexity is additional. This is an auditable exponential reference, not a polynomial-time implementation. The exact \(C=8\), \(m_2=6\) endpoint-envelope check enumerated all \(526\) feasible welfare-count vectors and attained probability \(37/1306368\) at counts \((1,0,0,0,6,0,0,0,1)\); it checks inherited arithmetic but is not used for coverage. The atom theorem rules out strict contained refinement only for \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\). It neither constructs nor excludes a consonant refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), and computing \(\delta_\star\) by exhaustive rational enumeration can itself be expensive.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The settled inferential results are exact simultaneous coverage, finite response-table compression, and the small-\(\alpha\) atom obstruction. The obstruction is global over all compatible pairs \((H,N)\), but it says only that a procedure cannot be strictly smaller at every nominal level while retaining uniform coverage: equality with the baseline is forced when \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\). Whether a consonant strict refinement exists at any level \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\) remains open. No shortness optimality, polynomial complexity, released calculator, or impossibility claim for the high-\(\alpha\) regime is made. Partial ties remain tied blocks of a complete weak order rather than being broken arbitrarily.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem supplies the finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantee for the causal weak order under the exact two-stage design.
statement_notes.gap: Existing generic rank methods require a simultaneous difference region, while nearby exact interference procedures target scalar or more sharply restricted nulls rather than the complete weak order of average quota-policy welfare.
statement_notes.consumer: RCT2 and the Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--Özler design calculator can report complete and tied policy orderings that remain compatible at level \(1-\alpha\).

statement_notes.justification: A minimum over the finite joint compatibility set turns the qualitative discreteness of the experiment into a strictly positive, computable global atom threshold.
statement_notes.gap: A table-specific atom does not support a uniform impossibility statement; the minimum must quantify jointly over every compatible observed table and every candidate response-count population.
statement_notes.consumer: Exact-order implementations can enumerate \(L_N(H)\) and report the threshold below which no valid contained shortening is possible.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives the faithful negative answer available for consonant closure: low-level strict refinement conflicts with uniform finite-sample coverage even without imposing consonance.
statement_notes.gap: The argument is deliberately silent for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), where a strict consonant exact construction may or may not exist.
statement_notes.consumer: Software designers can avoid searching for an impossible universal all-level refinement and can confine any closure search to nominal levels not excluded by the atom threshold.
